title: Apple Crumble
subtitle: Classic British baked apple dessert with a buttery oat topping
excerpt: Sweet, cinnamon-spiced apples under a rough, buttery crumble made with oats and honey. One of Britain's most loved puddings and one of the simplest to make.
sourceNotes: Apple crumble became popular in Britain during World War Two as a way of stretching pastry rations. The crumble topping uses less fat and flour than a pie crust and has remained the nation's preferred pudding format ever since.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Assemble up to 4 hours ahead. Bake just before serving.

content.text: Use cold butter and work it in quickly so the topping stays rubble-like, not a paste.

items.prepNote: peeled, cored, and sliced into 1cm pieces

content.text: Toss the apples with half the honey and half the cinnamon. Tip into a baking dish about 20x25cm.
For the topping, put the flour into a bowl with the remaining cinnamon.
Add the cold butter. Rub it in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles rough breadcrumbs. Some larger lumps are good.
Stir in the oats and the remaining honey. Toss until the mixture is lightly clumped.
Spread the topping evenly over the apples. Do not press it down.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until the topping is golden and the apple juices are bubbling at the edges.
Leave to cool for 5 minutes before serving with custard or cream.

items.cause: Oven runs cool or topping was packed too tightly.
items.fix: Raise heat to 190°C and bake for 5 to 10 more minutes.

items.cause: Slices were too thick or apples were very dense.
items.fix: Par-cook the apple filling on the hob for 5 minutes before topping.

items.symptom: Topping has sunk into the fruit.
items.cause: Too much juice from the apples.
items.fix: Pat apples dry before using; toss with a teaspoon of cornflour.
